item.title: Ratu Naiqama conveys best wishes to Navatu Secondary ahead of U19 Deans final
item.description: The Head of State and Na Gone Turaga Na Tui Cakau Ratu Naiqama Lalabalavu has conveyed his best wishes to the Navatu Secondary School Under-19 team as they prepare to take on Lelean Memorial School in Vodafone Fiji Secondary Schools Rugby Union Super Deans final today. item.content:encoded:
The Head of State and Na Gone Turaga Na Tui Cakau Ratu Naiqama Lalabalavu has conveyed his best wishes to the Navatu Secondary School Under-19 team as they prepare to take on Lelean Memorial School in Vodafone Fiji Secondary Schools Rugby Union Super Deans final today.

The Cakaudrove-based team visited State House, where they met Ratu Naiqama, who congratulated the team on their historic achievement and reminded the students of the importance of balancing their sporting commitments with their education.

He also highlighted the opportunities available through rugby, noting the significant contribution the sport has made to the livelihoods of many Fijians.

Navatu’s historic qualification for the Under-19 final marks a significant milestone for the school and is a proud moment for its students, families, supporters and the people of Cakaudrove.

Navatu Secondary will face Lelean at 2.20pm.

item.title: Bower set for Springboks clash as All Blacks name 23
item.description: Navitalai Naivalurua · 22/08/2026 George Bower has been named in the All Blacks' 23-member team that will face the Springboks in their first “Greatest Rivalry” tour match tomorrow morning.
item.content:encoded:
Navitalai Naivalurua · 22/08/2026

George Bower has been named in the All Blacks' 23-member team that will face the Springboks in their first “Greatest Rivalry” tour match tomorrow morning.

Bower has been named on the bench and will provide cover in the forwards.

Head coach Dave Rennie has recalled several star players, with Cam Roigard, Will Jordan and Damian McKenzie named in the starting side in Johannesburg.

The trio return from injury to take their places in the team, while Ardie Savea resumes the captaincy after being rested for the first three games of the South African tour.

Savea starts at number eight, with coach Dave Rennie retaining the loose-forward trio from last month's win against Ireland, with Luke Jacobson at openside flanker and Tupou Vaa'i at blindside.

Codie Taylor starts at hooker, with Tyrel Lomax and Ethan de Groot named as the starting props.

Rennie says they cannot wait to run out at Ellis Park tomorrow morning and, after all the build-up and anticipation, the entire touring squad is excited to get the first Test underway.

The All Blacks will face the Springboks at 3am tomorrow.

They will then play the second Test next Sunday at 3am, followed by the third Test on September 6th at 3am, with the fourth and final Test on September 13th at 3am.

item.title: Indiscipline costs Marist as they go down 17-15 to RKS in U15 Deans final
item.description: Indiscipline cost the Marist Brothers High School Under-15 side the Vodafone Fiji Secondary Schools Rugby Union Super Deans title as they went down 17-15 to Ratu Kadavulevu School this morning. Marist was leading 15-12 with a few minutes left to full time when they were handed a yellow card.
item.content:encoded:
Indiscipline cost the Marist Brothers High School Under-15 side the Vodafone Fiji Secondary Schools Rugby Union Super Deans title as they went down 17-15 to Ratu Kadavulevu School this morning.

Marist was leading 15-12 with a few minutes left to full time when they were handed a yellow card.

RKS grab the opportunity with both hands, and went forward, pushing for the try line.

RKS captain Josaia Sovau exploited the space in the corner, diving over to seal the win for his team.
